$purpose: Delivery is per account, not per device: messaging-service writes the same envelope to every
one of the recipient's per-device streams. When one message produces one ciphertext per
target device, every device receives all of them and must recognise which copy is its own —
cheaply, because a copy with message_number 0 that opens under no session takes the recovery
path and fetches a key bundle over the network for a message that was never its to read.
The tag answers that, and the relay cannot compute it even though it serves both public keys.
Two implementations of this that disagree do not produce an error. They produce a copy
discarded as foreign, a message that never appears, and no way to tell which side is wrong.
iOS carried the only implementation until 2026-08-25; it now lives in the core, and these
vectors are what keeps any future one honest.
The values below were produced by the iOS CryptoKit implementation BEFORE the port and then
asserted against the Rust one — a vector generated from the code it verifies proves nothing.

$construction.pair_secret: HKDF-SHA256(ikm = X25519(our_identity_private, peer_identity_public), salt = "ConstructSSTAG-v1", info = "") -> 32 bytes
why_the_target_is_in_the_mac: The pair secret alone is symmetric: A and B derive the same value, so a tag keyed on it
says 'this concerns A and B' and not which of the two it is for. Delivery hands the sender
its own copy back, so A would read its own echo as addressed to itself and try to open a
message it had just encrypted. Binding the target makes the tag directional while leaving
it opaque — the relay can compute neither direction.
$construction.base_message_id: the id WITHOUT any per-device or per-chunk suffix, so every chunk of one message carries one tag and the receiver can recompute it from whichever chunk arrives first
$construction.undecidable_is_not_foreign: a verifier must return 'does not match' rather than raising for unusable input, and callers must read that as 'not foreign': wrongly opening a copy costs failed decrypts, wrongly discarding one loses a message from the transcript, silently

note: Senders at or below iOS 0.18.0 wrote device_id[0..8] — the device id in plain hex, which the
relay could read on every copy it routed. The two forms are told apart by length alone,
which is why the current one is not also 8. Removal condition: no builds at or below 0.18.0
left in the field. A client comparing a full device id against a truncated tag by equality
rather than prefix discards every copy including its own.

keys.note: raw X25519 scalars; both X25519 implementations clamp on use, so the private bytes are pinned unclamped as a caller would supply them

vectors.name: same secret derived from the other side
tag for a copy A sends to device B
